title: Gene Calls with Prodigal
author: James Thornton
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.f47bqzn
materials: Make a directory named prodigal: $ mkdir prodigal

steps.title: Access HPC Cluster
steps.instruction: Log in to the HPC and move into the Cluster (ICE) environment.

steps.title: Navigate to Class Directory
steps.instruction: Change the current working directory to your specific class directory.

substeps.instruction: Execute: cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username (replacing 'username' with your actual username)

steps.title: Create Submission Script
steps.instruction: Create a new script named 'run-interactive.sh' containing the following PBS directives and bash header:

substeps.instruction: Include: #PBS -M netid@email.arizona.edu (replace netid with your own)

steps.title: Submit Interactive Job
steps.instruction: Submit the script interactively using the qsub command.

steps.title: Prepare Working Directories
steps.instruction: Once the job is ready, navigate to the directory containing the contigs.

substeps.instruction: Move to assembly directory: cd /rsgrps/bh_class/username/assembly (or the directory where final_contigs.fa is located, such as megahit-out)

steps.title: Run Prodigal for Gene Calling
steps.instruction: Load the Prodigal module and run it on the fixed_contigs.fa file to generate gene calls, protein sequences, and nucleotide sequences.

substeps.instruction: Note: Ensure you use fixed_contigs.fa (the file with simplified fasta header lines) and verify output paths to the prodigal directory

steps.title: Verify Gene Call Outputs
steps.instruction: Navigate to the prodigal output directory and verify that the gene calls were generated.

steps.title: Quantify Open Reading Frames
steps.instruction: Use scripting or Unix tools to determine the number of genes (ORFs) detected for each assembly.

substeps.instruction: Create a Google Documents table with a single column for '#ORFs'
List each sample name (e.g., 'SRR...') as a row and record the corresponding number of detected ORFs
